usageNotes: Returns the directory index for a specific task identified by its UPID on a PDM node — use this to discover what sub-resources are available under a task (e.g. log, status). The UPID must belong to the specified node; querying a UPID on the wrong node will return no results or an error. No special privilege is required beyond basic authentication (permissions: all users).

examples.summary: Get the directory index for a task UPID on pdm-node1

tips: The UPID format encodes node, PID, start time, task type, and user — copy it verbatim from a task-list response; do not construct it by hand.
This is a directory index, not a status or log endpoint — follow up with get_nodes_node_tasks_upid_status or get_nodes_node_tasks_upid_log to get actionable task data.
UPIDs are node-scoped; always use the same node name that appears inside the UPID string.
